policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Ketiv/qere orthographic pair of the same imperative of halak: qere lekah (with paragogic he) and ketiv lek are the identical word and identical in sense. ASV renders 'Come, I pray thee, with me unto another place', which reflects the imperative but cannot distinguish the spelling, and NUM.23.13 carries no ASV note mapped to this unit. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
